sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to below 1% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 4%; through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina lowers it to below 1%, non-anginal chest pain to about 1% and atypical angina to about 2% (chest pain type also acts through the non-anginal chest pain relay, below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: A reversible defect (or the undefined code 4) on the thallium scan raises it to about 44% and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 16%; higher cholesterol (from about 3% at 193 mg/dL to about 28% at 308 mg/dL) and higher resting blood pressure (from about 4% at 110 mm Hg to about 20% at 155 mm Hg) raise it steadily, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower.

Through this sum alone, each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same (from about 9% at 0 to about 75% at 2 vessels), a flat ST segment raises it to about 80%, and more ST depression raises it steadily, from about 5% at 0 mm to about 30% at 2.8 mm; all three also act through the parts below.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 2 and 15): through this sum alone an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG raises the risk to about 25%, and a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 1%; the model ignores age.

This part combines the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy with the maximum heart rate: through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, raising a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% at 0 to about 54% at 2 vessels.
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute.

It switches on when the number of vessels coloured plus about 0.036 × the maximum heart rate (in beats per minute) is above about 4.42, for a maximum heart rate from about 71 to 127 beats per minute; 227 of 242 training patients are on that side, and 44% of them had heart disease, against 47% of the others.

This part combines the number of vessels coloured with a flat ST segment and acts on 157 of 242 training patients, 95 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 99% without it and above 99% with it.
Through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, from about 9% at 0 to about 25% at 2 vessels for a typical patient, and a flat ST segment raises the risk from about 9% to about 14%.

Across the whole model, each extra vessel takes a typical patient from about 9% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, about the same for each, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher, and a flat ST segment takes it to about 87%.
This part reads only non-anginal chest pain: through it, non-anginal chest pain lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 2%.
Across the whole model, typical angina and non-anginal chest pain take it to below 1% and atypical angina to about 2%.

This part combines the resting ECG with ST depression on exercise and acts on 49 of 242 training patients, nearly all with a normal resting ECG, 31 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 99% without it and with it.

Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 1.0 mm, where this part switches on for patients with a normal resting ECG, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 9% at 0 mm to about 33% at 2.8 mm.

Across the whole model, ST depression therefore counts more with a normal resting ECG: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves a typical patient from about 5% to about 69%, rising slowly at first, then faster, against about 5% to about 31% otherwise.

Children add: +0.983*ca_slope2_gate (near-affine in ca, slope:2), -1.305*cp3_affine_relay (affine, -0.66 cp:3), +1.669*2245 and -0.165*2009 from ca_thalach_chain (mostly affine: +1.30 ca, small -thalach), and +1.335*normal_ecg_st_gate (the one real interaction: oldpeak adds extra risk only when restecg:0=+1). Composition is purely additive at node 0. Hypothesis (supported): the network is a logistic regression in which ca appears through three parallel affine routes (total ~+3.4 per SD), plus one gated ST-depression term. Evidence (train, n=242): AUC 0.939, acc 0.888. Replacing every ReLU by identity gives AUC 0.916, almost exactly the loss from removing only the 1801 ReLU (0.916), so 1801 is the only nonlinearity that matters; the other ReLUs change AUC by <=0.0002. Inputs age, sex:1, fbs:0, restecg:2, exang:1, slope:1, slope:3, thal:4, thal:7 are unconnected.

parts.original_hypothesis: Serial chain ca -> 2245 -> 2009 <- thalach. 2245 = ReLU(0.781*ca + 1.25) is always active on train (pre in [0.68, 3.31]); its readout +1.669 adds +1.30*ca + 2.08 to the logit (SD 1.30, the largest hidden contribution; mean-ablation costs 0.007 AUC). 2009 = ReLU(0.949*thalach + 1.36*2245 + 0.179) = ReLU(0.949*thalach + 1.06*ca + 1.87) is active on 93.8% of rows (clipped for 15 rows with very low max heart rate and few vessels); readout -0.165 gives a small -0.157*thalach - 0.175*ca term (SD 0.20). parts.name: ca_slope2_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Hidden node 664 = ReLU(0.601*ca + 0.326*slope:2 + 0.664), read out with +0.983. Hypothesis (supported): a near-affine risk term in number of major vessels coloured (ca) and flat ST slope (slope:2). On train the pre-activation ranges [-0.071, 2.607]; the ReLU clips only the 85 rows with ca at its minimum and slope:2=0, and only by <=0.071 (<=0.07 logit). Replacing the ReLU by identity leaves train AUC unchanged (0.9392 -> 0.9390); mean-ablating the node costs 0.002 AUC. Contribution SD 0.70 logit. So this is effectively +0.59*ca + 0.32*slope:2 added to the logit, on top of the direct ca and slope:2 edges.

parts.name: cp3_affine_relay
parts.original_hypothesis: Hidden node 1173 = ReLU(0.505*cp:3 + 1.92) is active on 100% of train rows (pre-activation in [1.59, 2.71]), so it is an affine relay: with readout -1.305 it contributes -0.658*cp:3 - 2.50 to the logit. Supported: line plot entry/exit correlation 1.0; removing the ReLU changes no prediction (AUC 0.9392 unchanged); mean-ablation costs 0.004 AUC. Meaning: non-anginal chest pain (cp:3) lowers predicted disease risk. cp:3 has no direct edge, so this is its only route to the output.

parts.name: normal_ecg_st_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Hidden node 1801 = ReLU(1.48*restecg:0 + 0.805*oldpeak - 1.43), readout +1.335. Hypothesis (supported): an interaction gate, the network's only consequential nonlinearity. restecg:0 takes values +/-1 (121 rows each on train). With restecg:0=+1 the gate passes ReLU(0.805*oldpeak + 0.05), active on 39.7% of those rows (exercise ST depression above about its median); with restecg:0=-1 it is active on 1/121 rows (needs oldpeak > 3.6 SD). So ST depression adds up to ~+3.4 extra logit, but only when restecg:0=+1. The ReLU matters: replacing it by identity drops train AUC 0.9392 -> 0.9162 (the linear version would add a large restecg:0 main effect); mean-ablating the whole node costs only 0.0001 AUC, so its value is the shape, not the extra ranking signal over the direct oldpeak edge (+0.869). Overall active rate 20%, contribution SD 0.55 logit.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

ann_30.text: This part acts on 157 of 242 training patients (65%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to above 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 95 of these 157 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 25% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 14%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient has non-anginal chest pain (about 2%) than if chest pain type is something other than non-anginal chest pain (about 9%) (on the training data only).

ann_32.text: This part acts on 49 of 242 training patients (20%); nearly all of them are patients with a normal resting ECG.
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to about 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 31 of these 49 patients had heart disease.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal (slowly at first, then faster for patients with a normal resting ECG): for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 5% to about 69% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 5% to about 31% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.

Other effects: ST depression on exercise past about 1.0 mm raises it with nothing until about 1.0 mm, then steadily; a higher ST depression on exercise raises it with nothing until about 1.0 mm, then steadily (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: any other resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 54% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

Through this part, the model treats a higher maximum heart rate as slightly lowering the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 10% at 118 beats per minute to about 8% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 87%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 80%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 75% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 5% at 0.0 mm to about 69% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

Other effects: any other thallium stress test result (rather than a normal thallium scan) raises it; a higher serum cholesterol raises it steadily; a higher ST depression on exercise raises it steadily; a higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily; an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) raises it; typical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; typical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; female (rather than male) lowers it; and 6 still smaller effects listed in the evidence table (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 2 training patients (an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (rather than fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less) lowers it; a higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way; signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) raises it (on the training data only).
